title: This Norwegian Strait Makes Whirlpools 33 Feet Wide

scenes.text: In Norway, the sea spins into giant whirlpools.
It's Saltstraumen, a gap only about 150 meters wide.
Every six hours, up to 400 million cubic meters of seawater squeeze through.
Some measurements put the current near 25 miles an hour.
At full strength it spins whirlpools up to 33 feet wide and 16 feet deep.
The sea doesn't just flow here. It spins.

description:

first_comment: Water at 25 miles an hour spinning into whirlpools. Would you sail through it?
